history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration include, in all future submissions to the Headquarters Committee on Contract for extensions of ICT contracts with a long duration (i.e., exceeding five years), an analysis of the potential advantages and disadvantages of such a long-term commitment.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. In response to the Board’s recommendation in paragraph 449 of its 2024 audit report (A/80/5 (Vol. I), the Office of Information and Communications Technology has completed a United Nations enterprise risk management-based vendor dependency assessment of all high- value ICT contracts, covering financial, operational, dependency and strategic risks, with formal mitigation and risk treatment plans documented. Where feasible, vendor lock-in and dependency risks are managed through technology diversification, contractual exit clauses and regular market benchmarking. Clear exit strategies and contingency arrangements have been established for all critical vendors. The workbook provided to the Board details procurement decision-making for high-value single-vendor contracts. The Office of Information and Communications Technology has also assessed single-vendor risks for high- value and long-tenure ICT contracts, working collaboratively with contract managers and category leads to determine risk levels and corresponding treatment plans. For the server, network and storage contract requirement, the Office has coordinated closely with the Procurement Division. The requirement has been split into five stand-alone solicitations, with ongoing work between Procurement Division buyers and requisitioners.
history.board_assessment: Given that a comprehensive assessment of single-vendor dependency across more than 10 high-value ICT contracts has been completed and the requirement has been broken down into five separate solicitation exercises, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
